title: Checking PA proofs inside arithmetic

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Construct the actual PA proof checker and verify its record-building operations at arbitrary internal codes.
abstract: What must Peano arithmetic prove before it can verify its own proof-building operations? We fix a numerical checker for its actual proof calculus and give finite certificates for its axioms, including induction with parameters. An arithmetic formula then expresses that this checker accepts a proposed proof. Combining proofs requires the conclusions, assumptions, axiom certificates, and fresh names to agree with the rule being applied. We verify these conditions for the constructors needed later, including modus ponens and specialization of a fixed theorem at numeral terms. The result provides uniform arithmetic proofs about those operations, rather than separate checks of ordinary proof codes.
